title: GitHub Actions Control-Plane Protocol Redesign v1
goal: Replace the current parser-chained GitHub Actions runner admission path with a formally modeled, versioned, typed control-plane protocol whose routing, authority, scheduling, provisioning, execution, recovery, and lifecycle semantics are explicit end-to-end, so any executor request admitted by policy cannot later be falsely rejected by a downstream parser that implements a different grammar.
acceptance_criteria: Produce an end-to-end protocol graph from GitHub trigger through workflow/job construction, scale-set messages, controller attestation, root admission, launch-spec resolution, JIT runner creation, execution, completion, cleanup, replay, and recovery.

Enumerate every parser, serializer, identifier, state machine, authority boundary, retry boundary, durable record, and scheduler/lifecycle signal in workspace-control and relevant research-engine workflows.
Classify each field as routing metadata, identity, authority claim, policy input, resource request, lifecycle state, evidence, or human-readable display only.
Eliminate authority-bearing free-form serialization in job display names. Human-readable job names may remain for audit but must not be the canonical protocol.

Define one canonical versioned request/envelope schema and one semantic interpretation of each field. Downstream layers may validate typed invariants but must not independently reinterpret the same user-controlled string grammar.

Define a protocol-compatibility rule: a request accepted at ingress either remains representable and valid through all downstream transitions or is rejected at ingress with a stable machine-readable reason.
Separate scheduling/liveness semantics from authority/policy semantics so policy rejection cannot crash-loop a scale-set listener.

Model JobAvailable, JobAssigned, JobStarted, JobCompleted, cancellation, reassignment, duplicate delivery, controller restart, provisioner restart, stale aggregate statistics, durable request replay, and cleanup failure explicitly.
Use the official GitHub Runner Scale Set Client lifecycle semantics rather than deriving scheduler state from ad hoc per-message counts.
Compare the design with GitHub ARC/Runner Scale Set Client, GitLab Runner taskscaler/fleeting, and Buildkite stack/queue architectures and document what is reused versus custom.
Define executor-facing policy contracts for workspace-control and research-engine so executors construct requests from schemas/enums/builders rather than hand-written slash-command strings.
Add generated/centralized builders and validators so workflow producers, controller tests, root-policy tests, and executor tooling derive from the same protocol specification.

Add property-based or exhaustive compatibility tests proving every admitted request variant traverses all parsers/validators without false rejection, and every invalid variant is rejected at the first authority boundary.
Add model/state-machine tests for duplicate delivery, retries, cancellations, queue backlog, start-limit, listener restart, and provisioner rejection.
No further Lambda control-plane mutation is allowed until the protocol graph, invariant set, migration plan, and repository-only compatibility suite are complete and accepted.
constraints: Do not treat individual parser failures as independent bugs unless the full protocol model proves they are independent.
Do not mutate Lambda, restart runner controllers, activate a new parser hotfix, or retrigger the blocked host-attest workflow while this redesign task is in architecture/research stages.
Do not start research-engine CPU/GPU controllers or alter research-engine quarantine/recovery state.
Do not replace GitHub's Runner Scale Set Client scheduling semantics with a custom queue/scheduler unless a documented capability gap requires it.
Keep root policy authority separate from GitHub credentials; redesign the evidence/envelope boundary rather than solving drift by giving root broad GitHub credentials.
Prefer typed structured data, exact identifiers, schemas, enums, generated builders, digests, and state machines over regex/string protocols.
Preserve fail-closed security boundaries, but policy rejection must be a recoverable job outcome, not a controller-fatal process outcome.
Keep GitHub-hosted validation available as a control path while the self-hosted control plane is redesigned.
